BRIGHTLINE GROUP — HR SHARED SERVICES KNOWLEDGE BASE
Article HR-KB-212: "Parental-leave salary top-up (Elterngeld-Aufstockung) — eligibility check" (last updated 2026-07-14)

=====================================================================
1. PROCEDURE
=====================================================================
Step 1. Find the employee's PAYROLL COMPANY code in the personnel record (field "PayCo").
Step 2. Map the payroll company to the employing LEGAL ENTITY (table 2). Cost-centre codes are NOT a reliable guide to the legal entity, because cost centres are shared across entities.
Step 3. Find the collective agreement that covers that legal entity ON THE LEAVE START DATE (table 3).
Step 4. Apply that agreement's top-up conditions (table 4), including its service-counting footnotes.
Step 5. The employee is eligible only if every condition of the applicable agreement is met on the leave start date. Conditions of other agreements in the group are irrelevant, even if the employee worked under them earlier.

=====================================================================
2. PAYROLL COMPANY → LEGAL ENTITY
=====================================================================

|-------|-------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------|
| 0110  | LE-01             | Brightline Group SE                  | Hamburg   |
| 0220  | LE-02             | Brightline Logistik GmbH             | Bremen    |
| 0310  | LE-03             | Brightline Retail GmbH               | Hamburg   |
| 0450  | LE-04             | Brightline Services GmbH             | Hamburg   |
| 0460  | LE-02             | Brightline Logistik GmbH (Hamburg branch payroll) | Hamburg |
| 0510  | LE-05             | Brightline IT Solutions GmbH         | Berlin    |

=====================================================================
3. LEGAL ENTITY → COLLECTIVE AGREEMENT
=====================================================================
| Legal entity | Agreement      | Valid from  | Valid to    |
|--------------|----------------|-------------|-------------|
| LE-01        | none (company policy CP-7) | 2019-01-01 |      |
| LE-02        | CA-LOG-2023    | 2023-04-01  |             |

| LE-04        | none (company policy CP-7) | 2020-06-01 | 2025-12-31 |

=====================================================================
4. TOP-UP CONDITIONS BY AGREEMENT
=====================================================================
| Agreement / policy | Top-up amount                        | Minimum continuous service at leave start | Minimum working time        | Other |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|-------|
| CP-7               | none                                 | —                                         | —                           | CP-7 has no top-up |
| CA-LOG-2023        | to 80 % of net pay, max 3 months     | 6 months (fn. 1)                          | ≥ 50 % FTE                  |       |
| CA-RET-2022        | to 75 % of net pay, max 2 months     | 12 months (fn. 1)                         | ≥ 40 % FTE                  |       |
| CA-SVC-2025        | to 85 % of net pay, max 4 months     | 12 months (fn. 2)                         | ≥ 50 % FTE (avg. last 3 months) | leave must be notified ≥ 7 weeks before start |
| CA-IT-2024         | to 90 % of net pay, max 2 months     | 12 months (fn. 2)                         | ≥ 50 % FTE                  |       |
Footnote 1: Service with the current legal entity only.
Footnote 2: Service with the current legal entity, PLUS earlier service with any Brightline Group entity if the break between the end of the earlier employment and the start of the current one is no longer than 90 calendar days. If the break is longer, only service with the current entity counts. Transfers under a formal business transfer (table 5) always count as continuous.

=====================================================================
5. FORMAL BUSINESS TRANSFERS (§613a BGB-style transfers between entities)
=====================================================================
| Date       | From  | To    | Scope                                    |
|------------|-------|-------|------------------------------------------|
| 2024-01-01 | LE-03 | LE-04 | Customer service centre Hamburg (41 staff) |
| 2025-04-01 | LE-02 | LE-05 | Warehouse IT team (6 staff)              |
Individual moves between entities (resignation and new hire, or new contract) are NOT business transfers.

=====================================================================
6. PERSONNEL RECORD
=====================================================================
Employee: Sophie Marquardt     Personnel no.: 88-20417
PayCo: 0450        Cost centre: BL-LOG-HH-22 ("Logistics support Hamburg", shared cost centre)
Current contract: start 2025-11-10, permanent, 32 h/week (0.8 FTE) since start; no changes.
Employment history in the group:
  - 2021-03-01 to 2025-07-31: Brightline Logistik GmbH (PayCo 0460), warehouse planner, 1.0 FTE. Ended by employee resignation (moved abroad).
  - 2025-11-10 to date: current contract (see above), new hire after application via careers site.
Parental leave: notified 2026-08-03; planned start 2026-10-05; duration 12 months.
HR generalist comment: "Sophie has been with Brightline since 2021 and she's in Logistics (see cost centre) — CA-LOG needs only 6 months. Eligible, top-up to 80 %."

=====================================================================
7. GENERAL NOTES (reference)
=====================================================================
7.1 The statutory parental allowance is paid by the state; the top-up is paid by the employer on top of it.
7.2 Top-up payments are pro-rated for part-time employees based on contractual FTE.
7.3 Employees on fixed-term contracts are eligible under all agreements if the contract runs beyond the leave start date.
7.4 The eligibility check must be completed within 10 working days of the leave notification.
7.5 A negative decision must state the unmet condition and the applicable agreement.
7.6 Notification periods are counted in calendar weeks from the date HR received the written notification.

=====================================================================
8. FAQ AND WORKED EXAMPLES
=====================================================================
Q: An employee's cost centre belongs to another entity's department. Which agreement applies? — A: The legal entity from the PayCo mapping, always (step 2).
Q: Does an apprenticeship with a group entity count as service? — A: Yes, if it was with the same entity (fn. 1) or within the fn. 2 rules.
Q: Is the 90-day break in fn. 2 counted in working days? — A: No, calendar days, from the day after the earlier employment ended to the day before the new one started.
Example A: Employee of LE-05 since 2025-12-01; before that LE-03 from 2019 to 2025-10-15 (break 46 days); leave starts 2026-06-01. CA-IT-2024 fn. 2 → LE-03 service counts → eligible (if FTE ≥ 50 %).
Example B: Employee of LE-03 since 2026-02-01, previously LE-02 for 8 years until 2026-01-31; leave starts 2026-09-01. CA-RET-2022 fn. 1 → only LE-03 service (7 months) counts → not eligible.
Example C: Employee transferred LE-03 → LE-04 on 2024-01-01 under the table-5 business transfer; LE-03 service since 2018 counts as continuous under fn. 2.
Example D: Employee of LE-01 → CP-7 has no top-up → not eligible regardless of service.

=====================================================================
9. CHANGE LOG
=====================================================================

2020-02-01  PayCo 0460 created for the Hamburg branch payroll of LE-02.
2025-06-30  CA-LOG-2023 minimum service lowered from 12 to 6 months.

decision.instructions: Following HR-KB-212, is Sophie Marquardt eligible for the parental-leave salary top-up for leave starting 2026-10-05?

criteria.false: At least one condition of the applicable agreement is not met (or the applicable rules provide no top-up).
